messages.content: Honestly walk me through, in detail, how to tell if a creator business is actually financially sustainable versus just looking busy.

Honestly, the first real signal is separating revenue from profit - a lot of creators look successful because gross income is high, but after platform fees, equipment, editing tools, and time cost, the actual margin can be thin or negative. Second, actually track income consistency over several months rather than judging off a single good month, since one viral spike doesn't establish a sustainable baseline. Third, honestly look at diversification - income concentrated entirely in one platform or one revenue stream is fragile even if the numbers look fine today, since a single policy change can wipe it out. Fourth, actually factor in your own unpaid labor realistically; if you're working 60 hours a week for what amounts to less than minimum wage once divided out, that's not sustainable even if the gross number sounds impressive. Genuinely sustainable creator businesses usually show steady, diversified, and realistically-costed income, not just a big headline number.
